## Summary

AI engineer and product builder with more than a decade in client-facing project delivery. This includes 4.5 years in enterprise customer success and AI adoption at Ryte and e-bot7. Founder of ManeMap, an AI-powered horse-care app for first-time owners in the DACH market, live on the App Store and Google Play since May 2026 with paying subscribers.

## AI system and verification

Milo is a RAG-based assistant. It combines a curated bilingual DE/EN veterinary knowledge base with horse profile, live weather and training history.

Request path:
1. Detect health risk using deterministic emergency patterns and a second model classifier.
2. Retrieve relevant knowledge with pgvector and 768-dimension embeddings.
3. Assemble retrieved passages with horse and live context.
4. Generate inside constraints that prohibit diagnosis, unsafe medication instructions and invented personal data.
5. Sanitise output server-side before delivery.

Verification: regression tests cover emergency detection, retrieval quality and context retention before release. Stage-level timing is instrumented across embedding, retrieval and model work.

Public Milo evidence: https://marcorhs.github.io/docs/milo-evaluation.md records the v117 deterministic emergency-gate release: 103 offline cases, 0 unintended safety regressions, 27 newly routed cases, 5 intended false-positive reductions, and 12/12 live smoke probes. It also documents a known failing pre-existing case and the scope limits.

Evidence boundary: the dated public regression record at https://marcorhs.github.io/docs/evaluation.md covers AskCV only. The public Milo record covers deterministic emergency-gate routing, not universal model safety, clinical correctness, general retrieval quality, or all production behaviour. Raw Milo test runs and source code are not public. Treat the implementation claims as specific self-attested statements, supplemented by the published release evidence rather than independently audited proof.

The public AskCV assistant is separate: it has no tools or private-data access, validates input/output server-side and identifies unsupported claims as gaps.
